s.note: the tea party on the ceiling with Uncle Albert
s.how: Spread white bread with cream cheese and layer with thin cucumber. Mash 4 hard-boiled eggs with salt and spread with mustard cress. Fill more with ham and a little mustard. Cut off the crusts, slice into fingers and stack on a tiered plate.

Mix 400g finely diced chuck steak with 250g diced potato, 150g diced swede, 1 diced onion, 1 tsp salt and plenty of pepper. Cut 4 x 20cm rounds from 4 sheets of shortcrust pastry. Pile the filling onto one half of each, dot with butter, fold over and crimp the edge. Brush with beaten egg, cut a small slit and bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 170C for 40 minutes. Serve with brown sauce.

m.note: Sunday at the Banks house on Cherry Tree Lane
m.how: Roast a 1.5kg beef topside at 200C to medium and rest. Whisk 150g flour, 3 eggs and 300ml milk into a batter and bake in hot oiled muffin tins for 20 minutes. Roast 1kg potatoes alongside, cook peas and make gravy with pan juices and stock.

w.note: Mary and Bert jumping into the chalk pavement drawing
w.how: Dissolve 150g sugar in 150ml hot water and cool. Blend 500g raspberries with the syrup and the juice of a lemon, then strain out the seeds. Freeze in a tray, scraping with a fork every hour for 4 hours. Serve in glass dishes with ice cream wafers.

d.note: Admiral Boom firing his cannon from the rooftop on Cherry Tree Lane
d.how: Simmer 100g caster sugar, 100ml water and a 6cm piece of sliced ginger for 10 minutes, then cool and strain. Rub the rims of 4 glasses with lemon and dip in caster sugar. Fill with ice and add 3 tbsp ginger syrup and the juice of a quarter lemon to each. Top with soda water and stir. Garnish with a strip of crystallised ginger.
